newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Trading of China Res shares suspended.
newsitem.headline: Trading of China Res shares suspended.

text.p: Trading in shares of China Resources Enterprise Ltd was suspended late Tuesday morning at the company's request pending an announcement, the Hong Kong stock exchange said.
Trade in China Resources' derivative warrant was also suspended, the exchange said.
The shares were last traded at HK$12.95 per share, up HK$0.95 or 7.92 percent from Monday closing. Volume was 3.62 million shares worth HK$44.99 million.
The warrants were last traded up HK$0.14 at HK$0.80.
Brokers said the suspension was rumoured to be related to a possible share placement which the company was said to be planning to fund an investment in a shipping terminal operator.
"I heard that it (the suspension) is related to a placement of 460 million new shares by the company at HK$10.87 per share," said a sales manager at a regional brokerage.
China Resources officials were not immediately available for comment.

China Resources' parent, China Resources (Holdings) Co Ltd, is the second largest shareholder of Hongkong International Terminal (HIT), which is 77.5 percent owned by Hutchison Whampoa Ltd as in June.
Analysts said China Resources (Holdings) holds about 10 percent of HIT and speculated China Resources Enterprise may be planning to take over the stake.
